facts.text: Howard Beach was founded in 1897 by William J. Howard, a glove maker who turned his 150‑acre goat farm into a seaside community.
The Long Island Rail Road opened the Ramblersville station in 1905, a name that later became the basis for the Howard Beach – JFK Airport station.
Folk legend Woody Guthrie called Howard Beach home, living at 159‑13 85th Street after leaving Coney Island.
The neighborhood’s quiet, low‑rise homes were shaped by Howard’s original cottages and a hotel that burned in 1907.
Howard Beach’s proximity to Idlewild Airport—renamed JFK in 1963—brought both convenience and noise, yet the community’s strong civic networks kept its small‑town feel.
The Queens Public Library’s Howard Beach branch, located at 92‑06 156th Avenue, serves the neighborhood’s residents with a long history of community learning.
